title: Adapting scientific streaming inference workflows for a deterministic tensor processing unit
problem: Real-time data processing near X-ray detectors is constrained by long ASIC development cycles and limited computational capacity of near-detector FPGAs, creating a bottleneck for time-sensitive photon science experiments.
motivation: Scientific facilities require low-latency, high-throughput inference at the edge to enable experimental-in-the-loop computing and intelligent control in real-time X-ray imaging systems.
method: The researchers set up a hybrid system that streams X-ray detector data directly to a Groq accelerator, a specialized processor designed for fast, predictable computation. Using a supporting software stack, the Groq processor performs image analysis with minimal delay (low-latency inference), which is critical since X-ray detectors generate data faster than traditional approaches can handle. The system integrates these results back into photon science workflows, giving scientists real-time feedback from their experiments.
key_novelty: Streaming X-ray image analysis using a deterministic tensor processor (Groq) at the edge achieves microsecond-level latency, matching high-speed detector data rates.
contributions: System architecture for streaming X-ray data to deterministic TPU
156.06 microseconds latency for 128x128 image inference (including transfer time)
3.6x speedup over previous systems for edgePtychoNN model
6.4 kHz processing capability enabling experimental-in-the-loop computing
limitations: Limited to single detector type (X-ray ptychography); deterministic TPU deployment limited to Groq availability; scalability to larger image resolutions not discussed.
